rows.38:2f7c:
Once, when I went on a trip, I saw a famous old cherry tree.
It was mid-April, I think?
From its huge, ancient trunk, far too big for one person to get their arms around, drooping branches hung down and spread out in every direction, and every single one of them was packed with blossoms, without a gap.
It was like a curtain of cherry blossoms.
I just stood under the flowers, gazing up in a daze...
That was when I heard a voice.
It really did seem to come from the old cherry tree.
I felt drawn to it, and when I went up to the old tree and put my ear against it...{p}
rows.38:3160:
Mixed in with a sound like water and nutrients flowing through the inside of the trunk, there was a voice.
"I'm so tired now.
Please, won't you let me rest?"
That's what I heard it say.
I was startled and looked all around, but there was no one there.
Then I looked down at the old tree's trunk, and there were countless nutrient injections jabbed into it.{p}
rows.38:32a8:
Sure, that old tree has lived far, far longer than an ordinary cherry tree's lifespan.
But I think the tree had grown tired of having that much done to it just to keep it alive.
For a person, I think it'd be the same as not being able to live without drugs and life-support machines.
I felt sorry for that tree, but there was nothing I could do...
You're saying I just imagined it?
No, that's not true.
I heard it clearly, with my own ears.
Maybe it wasn't so much the tree itself as the voice of the spirit dwelling in it, don't you think?
Ever since that happened, there's one thing I've been sure of.
Yes, that flowers and trees have spirits dwelling in them...
So if you insult them, show them horrible sights, treat them carelessly or handle them roughly... even plants get angry.
Well, that old cherry tree was well cared for, so I don't think that would happen to it.{p}
rows.38:35b0:
Hmm. But you do like flowers, right?
As a flower lover, I can't forgive anyone who doesn't like cherry blossoms.
That's practically heresy.
Me, out of all the flowers, I really love cherry blossoms.{p}
rows.38:3658:
You're scared?
So you're quite the scaredy-cat, huh.
But you know, you see it a lot, right?
Trees growing smack in the middle of a road, or buildings built to avoid one spot because the tree there couldn't be cut down...
That has to be because there's some reason behind it, right?
They all have in common that nobody can cut the tree down, but I think the story behind each one is different.{p}
rows.38:3798:
So, about that cherry tree, aren't you a little curious?
Trees are smart, see, so a normally grown tree won't get angry or get in the way once you get it to understand the situation.
When accidents happen, it's either because nobody properly explained the situation to the tree, or because an evil spirit dwells in it.
That's what I think.
But you know, they did properly explain the situation to that tree.
They even told it they were only moving it somewhere else, and would never hurt it.
That's what I heard.{p}
rows.38:394c:
But if it still wouldn't accept that, then maybe an evil spirit really does dwell in it.
There are all kinds of rumors about that cherry tree.
I'll tell you one.
It's from back when the old school building was still in use.
That said, I guess by then the tree was already pretty old...
It was an ordinary cherry tree that bloomed ordinary flowers.{p}
rows.38:3a94:
Back then, there was a first-year named Miyuki Tojo, a quiet girl, the type who didn't have many friends.
But she wasn't gloomy at all.
There was a reason for that.
She had a close friend.{p}
rows.38:3b70:
Her friend was that very cherry tree, they say.
You think that's ridiculous?
Yeah, it is ridiculous, but they were all kids from the old days, right?
It seems everyone just thought she was a romantic.
Back then, even if a kid was a little different from everyone else, I don't think there was the kind of awful bullying there is now...
In the morning, when she got to school, she'd say good morning to the tree; at break she'd go to see it, she ate her lunch there, and after school she stayed by the tree until the school gate closed.
Whether it rained or snowed, or on the hottest days of midsummer, always...
They say she'd sit at the foot of the tree, always happily murmuring to herself.
I don't know if that was why, but they say it bloomed beautifully every year.
Maybe her feelings got through to the tree...
I hear a photographer even came once to take pictures of it.
And so two peaceful years went by, until one day, not long before graduation.{p}
rows.38:3e88:
A classmate saw her under that cherry tree with another figure, they say.
And it was a boy, too.
"Who knew Tojo was so fast? You can't judge by looks.
I wonder if she's been meeting him there in secret all along."
That rumor went around.
But the truth was different.
The classmate really had seen her with a boy, but right at that moment, he was confessing his feelings to her.{p}
rows.38:4008:
She agonized over it.
Not that there was anything wrong with him...
Why, you ask?
She and the cherry tree, through being together, had come to have feelings for each other beyond friendship.
You're asking if she was crazy?
I told you before, didn't I?
Plants have feelings... spirits dwell in them...{p}
rows.38:4144:
I bet people who love plants, or who are very sensitive, or who have a strong sixth sense, can talk to trees.
When he confessed to her, I guess she finally realized, don't you think?
That she was a human, and the one she loved was a cherry tree...
After that, there were classmates who said they'd seen her crying under the tree...
You know how there are girls who are huge{g}fans of some idol and follow him everywhere, but then they get a real boyfriend and wake up to reality?
The object was different, but it was the same for her.
It seems she told the tree that once she graduated, she wouldn't be able to stay by its side anymore.
And that she'd fallen for someone, too...{p}
rows.38:4424:
"So this really is goodbye...
You'll be all right without me now, won't you?"
Then she gently leaned against the tree's trunk.
She closed her eyes,{p}
rows.38:44c4:
"Was this tree always this warm?
I can hear something flowing inside the trunk.
...Just like a person.
Like this, it's as if I'm wrapped in the scent of cherry blossoms,"
she murmured.
Little by little, the western sky turned red, and in the east, stars came out...
Was it just her imagination that the sky felt closer than usual?
Little by little, her mind drifted away...{p}
rows.38:461c:
The next morning, they say a shoe with Tojo's name written on it was lying at the foot of the cherry tree.
And strangely, the tree was in full bloom.
Tojo went missing after that, and her classmates all said she'd been swallowed up by that cherry tree...
That tree just had to keep her from leaving, no matter what.
If so, it thought, they might as well become one...
Her consciousness, once it was taken in, was only a part of the tree at first, but before anyone knew it, it took over the whole tree, and in the end it became the tree itself, don't you think?{p}
rows.38:4838:
If you go near that tree at dusk, you know,
"Notice me... I'm right here."
They say you can hear a whisper like that.
That's probably why it keeps refusing even to be moved.
Yeah, more than an evil spirit, I think it's her strong feelings at work, and that's one of the reasons nobody can persuade the tree.
That tree is behind the old school building, so not many people see it, but its blossoms are a deeper color than normal cherry blossoms.
From far away, it looks like a red mist.
That's the end of my story.
Okay, next person, go ahead...{p}
rows.38:4a28:
You've got a death wish, huh?
If you cut that tree down now, something terrible would happen.{p}
rows.38:4a7c:
Huh?
You're saying you just don't believe in that kind of thing?
But you actually see it around, right?
Trees growing smack in the middle of a road, or buildings built to avoid one spot because the tree there couldn't be cut down...
That has to be because there's some reason behind it, right?
I'm sure each one has its own story, but they're all the same in that nobody can cut the tree down.
In the case of that cherry tree...{p}
rows.38:4bc8:
...This is from back when the old school building was still in use.
Of course, there was no new school building yet, and I don't think the old building was so run-down back then.{p}
rows.38:4c6c:
Back then, there was a boy at this school named Asakura.
Asakura was cheerful, good at sports, and cool...
In other words, he was like every girl's dream guy, they say.
Not that I saw him myself.
And he was what you'd call the outdoorsy type these days, I guess; he loved the mountains and the sea.{p}
rows.38:4d78:
Trees and flowers can tell when someone's like that.
Plants loved him.
Did you know?
They say people have compatibility with plants, too.
He seems to have been the type plants love unconditionally.
Liked not just by his classmates and teachers but by plants too... I'm a little jealous.{p}
rows.38:4e84:
Asakura apparently used to nap or read books under that cherry tree a lot.
He must have liked being near trees.
And that cherry tree liked him too, just like the other plants did.
In spring it put out gorgeous blossoms, in summer it made cool shade... it did its best to make him happy like that.
...But happiness never lasts long, does it?{p}
rows.38:4fcc:
One day, Asakura got sick.
At first, everyone thought it was just a cold.
He'd always been really healthy until then, so he didn't worry about it much himself.
But that was the mistake.
He came down with a lung disease and moved away to the countryside, where the air was better, to recover.
He really hated leaving this place...
Being sick had made him weak-hearted, too; he must have been lonely.
But he and his classmates weren't the only ones who were sad.{p}
rows.38:5174:
They say that cherry tree, too, scattered its petals as it watched the car drive away...
...After that, the tree never saw Asakura again.
They say he died at the hospital where he went to recover...
"If I may wish, let me die in spring beneath the blossoms."
It's a famous line, right?
Those were his last words.
The blossoms there mean cherry blossoms, right?
He really did want to come back, didn't he?{p}
rows.38:52a0:
That day... the tree was scattering its petals, just like on the day it saw Asakura off...
They say it was just like tears.
What's wrong, {c}{f:|}?
Ahahaha, you want to say it's not scary at all, right?
I know.
The scary part starts here.
Yeah, up until then, the tree was just like any other gentle, ordinary tree.
But from the moment Asakura died, it changed.{p}
rows.38:5408:
Right now, that cherry tree is calling for Asakura with all its heart and soul.
Because it knows perfectly well that he wanted to come back...
You know what spirit paths are, right?
They're the routes ghosts travel along, and they say they exist all over the place.
That cherry tree is pulling those spirit paths toward itself.
Waiting for the day Asakura passes along one of them...
And while it did that, before it knew it, lots of spirits ended up dwelling in the tree.
Just like the roads we use every day have sidewalks, roadways and one-way streets, they say there are all kinds of spirit paths too.
Paths that lead to heaven.
Paths that lead to hell.
Paths that loop around so you can never get out.
Paths that good spirits travel.
Paths that evil spirits travel.
That's about it, to keep it simple.{p}
rows.38:5698: Hey, {c}{f:|}.{p}Which spirit path do you think that tree is pulling in?
rows.38:570c: I'd like to believe no spirit path runs through there
rows.38:5738:
Are you still saying that?
Sorry, but spirit paths do run through it.
And not just one or two, either.
I mean, Asakura died way off in the countryside, remember?
Even that tree couldn't make a path connecting there to here.
So it's pulling in every spirit path around it, whatever it can get.
This school has creepy spots all over the place, right?
So many spirit paths have been warped that space itself has gone strange.
But where could Asakura's spirit be, I wonder?
Maybe he still can't find his way to the tree?
Or maybe...
Maybe he forgot all about the tree and passed on...
Even if Asakura could meet the tree now, I think it'd already be too late.{p}
rows.38:599c:
Because that tree is full of the grudges of all kinds of spirits.
Strong spirits and weak spirits are all lumped in together.
The spirit world is survival of the fittest too, and weak spirits get eaten.
Though apparently ordinary spirits don't do that, so the ones doing the eating would have to be powerful evil spirits.
That's how they keep getting stronger and stronger.{p}
rows.38:5ad8:
Get it now?
Why that tree can't be moved...
Cutting it down? No way! Right?
Leaving it like this is definitely dangerous too, but it'll hold out at least until we graduate.
That's only a guess, though...
Probably.
Maybe that's irresponsible, but I'm just a normal high school girl, not a psychic.
There's no way I could purify that tree with a half-baked sixth sense.
I'd just end up getting swallowed by the grudges.
Or do you still not believe it?
The grudges being carved into that tree...
If you want, we can go and look.{p}What do you say?
rows.38:5d00:
Oh, now you're just saying whatever suits you.
But, yeah, you're right.
The path that tree was pulling in was the one traveled by spirits trying to properly pass on.
Calling them good or bad is kind of strange, but they say the most important thing a spirit needs is the will to move.
No matter how harmless a spirit is, if it just stays put and does nothing, it's beyond saving, they say.
And I don't sense much malice from the spirit path itself, so I think it's just a normal, perfectly ordinary spirit path.{p}
rows.38:5f54:
All it can think about is calling Asakura, so it can't set the other spirits free.
I wonder how the trapped spirits feel?
Sad, or bitter, I bet.
It wouldn't be strange if that slowly turned into resentment and hatred, would it?
And those grudges are slowly taking over the tree...{p}
rows.38:6090:
Hey, let's go look at it now.
I'll prove to you that my story isn't a lie.{p}Come on, okay?
rows.38:6170:
...The area around the old school building really is creepy, isn't it?
Especially out back here where this tree is; even in the daytime it's gloomy, and it feels damp, don't you think?
It's not like it doesn't get any sun, either.
I guess it's the atmosphere.{p}
rows.38:6244:
Look, there it is.
The white blossoms are in full bloom.
It's scary, though, isn't it?
This tree is in bloom all year round...
Huh?
That's weird...?
I thought this tree had redder blossoms than that...
Well?
After hearing the story, it's even creepier, right?
You know why they say there are dead bodies buried under cherry trees? It's because if you cut a cherry tree's trunk before it blooms, red sap flows out.
Come on, don't stand so far away.
Take a closer look.{p}
rows.38:63dc:
That scar near the bottom of the trunk is from when they tried to cut it down before, and they say red sap came pouring out then too.
I guess part of it was that it creeped them out, but I really don't think this tree is normal.{p}
rows.38:64b0:
Hey, look closely at these blossoms.
They're white today, so it should be easy to tell, but in the middle of each flower, look...{p}
rows.38:6528:
You can see a face, right?
More like a skull than a face, maybe?
See? Every blossom has a creepy stain on it.
These must be the grudges of the spirits this tree has absorbed.{p}
rows.38:65d0:
What's wrong?
{c}{f:|}, you're shaking.
Are you scared?{p}Want to go back to the club room?
rows.38:6624: I want to go back to the club room
rows.38:6634: No, I want to stay here a while longer
rows.38:6654:
Heh heh, you're just putting on a brave face.
But take responsibility for what you said, okay?
I'm scared, so I'm going back to the club room.
You can look at the tree as long as you like, {c}{f:|}.
See you later, then.{p}If you take too long, I'll go home without you.
rows.38:6748:
Huh, what?
You're scared to be alone?
Oh, all right, just a little longer, then.
If you still want to stay here, that means you sensed something, right?
The grudges squirming inside this tree, maybe?
I can't tell that much myself.
All I get is a vague sense of something hazy, some kind of unknowable presence.{p}So, so, did you see something?

notes: 38:44c4: last two lines are Miyuki's free indirect thoughts in Japanese present tense; rendered in past tense third person ('her imagination', 'her mind drifted away').
